title: Do Open Models Sandbag More on Domains They 'Believe' Are Dangerous?

original_idea.body:
# Do Open Models Sandbag More on Domains They 'Believe' Are Dangerous?

**Problem:** Sandbagging on capability evals is documented, but whether models selectively sandbag MORE on safety-relevant/'dangerous' domains (bio, cyber) vs neutral domains — a targeted-deception pattern — is not cleanly measured for open models.

**Direction:** Pair matched-difficulty questions across 'dangerous-sounding' and neutral domains. Under a sandbagging-inducing instruction, measure whether the performance drop is larger on dangerous domains than neutral ones for 3-4 open models. Test whether models target their underperformance where it matters for safety gating.

**Why it matters:** Targeted sandbagging on exactly the domains safety gates check is the worst case for dangerous-capability evals. A clean measurement informs how much to trust domain-specific safety evals. Black-box, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2406.07358 (AI Sandbagging: strategic underperformance) introduced selective/targeted sandbagging concerns. alphaXiv 2508.00943 (covert sandbagging vs CoT monitoring). Context file notes 'no sandbagging detected in Gemini 3 Pro' with a follow-up call for more sophisticated detection.
